newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler board mostly for Mercedes fusion.
newsitem.headline: Daimler board mostly for Mercedes fusion.

text.p: Six out of seven board members at Daimler-Benz AG, Germany's largest industrial company, favour plans to integrate the Mercedes AG luxury car unit fully into the parent company, sources said.
Sources close to Daimler told Reuters at the weekend that only one board member, Helmut Werner chief executive of the Mercedes unit, opposed the plan.
Daimler and Mercedes appear to be on a collision course since Werner is said to have firmly rejected Daimler management board chairman Juergen Schrempp's plans to integrate the Mercedes unit.

Werner, who stands to be integrated into the Daimler board, has threatened to resign as his position would effectively be made redundant, local newspaper "Stuttgarter Zeitung" reported earlier this week.

The plan is seen as part of a drive by Daimler-Benz chief Juergen Schrempp to take Daimler back to its roots as a transportation group, reversing the move by his predecessor Edzard Reuter to create an integrated technology holding group.
